title: Which of the earlier angles are acute, right, obtuse or straight?
description: An L shaped paper corner is laid on the three groups of angles and the notebook cover that Ruhee opens flat. The corner shows which angles are smaller, equal or bigger than a right angle, and the flat cover shows the straight angle. The check lines the four kinds up in order of size.
teaching_notes: One idea: compare each angle with a right angle, and a straight angle has its arms in one line. Watch for children who leave the straight angle out because it looks like a line.

video_script.why: The child names each earlier angle by comparing it with a right angle, and spots the straight angle.
video_script.substitution: The book's own three groups of angles and the notebook cover opened flat.
video_script.anchor: the book's three groups of angles and the notebook cover that Ruhee opens flat on the table
video_script.payoff_line: The left group is acute and the middle group is right. The right group is obtuse, and the flat cover is a straight angle.

final_answer.value: left group acute, middle group right, right group obtuse; the cover opened flat is a straight angle
final_answer.spoken: the left group is acute, the middle group is right, the right group is obtuse, and the flat cover is a straight angle

names.Ruhee: book character who opens the cover of a notebook a half turn onto the table

maths_rules: left group: every angle fits inside the L shaped corner, smaller than a right angle, acute
middle group: every angle matches the corner exactly, right
right group: every angle is wider than the corner but narrower than a straight angle, obtuse
the cover opened flat has its arms in one line, a half turn, a straight angle
a straight angle holds two right angles, so it is bigger than every obtuse angle
video_script.design: The three groups of the book and the open cover stay on the board. One amber corner moves over them, the same way as in the solved example.

narration: <bookmark mark='ell'/>A right angle looks like the letter L, and it is a quarter turn.
<bookmark mark='kinds'/>An angle smaller than a right angle is called acute. An angle bigger than a right angle but smaller than a straight angle is called obtuse.
<bookmark mark='line'/>Two arms lying in one line make a straight angle. It is a half turn.
